jobs.title: Sales Manager
jobs.description:
You'll lead Luma's regional sales — owning strategic accounts yourself while hiring and coaching a team of Account Executives — and place our creative AI technology with the world's leading brands and agencies. This is a player-coach role.

You'll both close deals and build the team, refining the regional playbook in a high-velocity, ambiguous environment rather than following a set one. It fits a deeply networked sales leader who still wants to sell, not just manage. If you want a pure management seat or an established playbook, this isn't it.

What You'll Own

 - Own the full sales cycle for strategic accounts — prospecting, demos, and closing high-impact deals with leading brands and agencies.

 - Hire, mentor, and lead a team of 5+ Account Executives with day-to-day coaching and a culture of excellence.

 - Build and manage a robust pipeline of advertiser and agency accounts.

 - Translate Luma's creative AI tools into clear value and ROI for marketing, brand, and creative teams.

 - Partner with marketing, product, and customer success to refine the go-to-market motion and feed insight back to product.

 - Refine the foundational playbooks that grow the regional footprint.

First 90 Days

One way the first 90 could unfold.

 - Days 1–30 — Immerse & Diagnose: Learn the product and region, and start closing strategic accounts yourself.

 - Days 30–60 — Ship & Validate: Close early deals and begin building the team.

 - Days 60–90 — Scale & Systemize: Grow the AE team and refine the regional playbook.

What You Bring

 - 8+ years of sales with a track record of exceeding quota, ideally selling creative/marketing tools, MarTech, or media.

 - 3+ years of recent sales management, hiring and leading sales professionals.

 - Deeply networked in the region's advertising, brand, and agency ecosystem, with an active Rolodex of decision-makers.

 - A player-coach who'll close deals today and scale a team, comfortable with ambiguity in early-stage growth.

 - Based in the region, or willing to relocate.

Nice to Have

 - Experience at a high-growth generative AI, media, AdTech, or creative-technology startup (Runway, Pika, Jasper).

 - A deep passion for creative AI and a strong understanding of multimodal technology.

 - Experience navigating complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise cycles with creative directors and agency holdcos.

Note: this body covers Sales Manager - West Coast (LA/SF Bay Area) and Sales Manager - East Coast (New York) — localize the region and network language per posting.

About Luma: Luma's mission is to build unified general intelligence that can generate, understand, and operate in the physical world. We believe multimodality is critical for intelligence — the next step beyond language models comes from vision. Luma is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Senior Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
You'll own a portfolio of Luma's high-value enterprise accounts and be responsible for growing how much they use the platform and how far it spreads inside their organizations. The role blends commercial ownership, product usage, and customer strategy.

Luma's post-sales organisation is early, so you'll help set how account growth is driven across EMEA rather than inheriting a mature motion. It fits someone commercial who's fluent with usage data and comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous environments. If you want a defined playbook and steady accounts to maintain, this isn't that.

What You'll Own

 - Own a portfolio of strategic enterprise accounts, responsible for expansion and long-term growth.

 - Find and execute opportunities to grow usage across teams, geographies, and use cases.

 - Build multi-threaded relationships across technical, operational, and executive stakeholders.

 - Own and interpret usage data, spotting trends, spikes, and drop-offs across accounts.

 - Turn usage insight into proactive growth strategies.

 - Partner with product and engineering to unlock new use cases and clear adoption blockers.

 - Lead account planning, expansion strategy, and commercial conversations, and contribute to renewals.

First 90 Days

One way the first 90 could unfold.

 - Days 1–30 — Immerse & Diagnose: Learn your accounts, their usage patterns, and where adoption is stuck.

 - Days 30–60 — Ship & Validate: Land an expansion or new-use-case win in a priority account, driven by usage data.

 - Days 60–90 — Scale & Systemize: Turn the approach into a repeatable account-growth motion for EMEA.

What You Bring

 - 5–10+ years in Strategic Account Management, Enterprise Sales, or commercial Customer Success in SaaS, AI, or enterprise tech.

 - A track record of driving expansion and growth in large, complex accounts.

 - Strong commercial mindset and comfort working with data, dashboards, and usage metrics.

 - Ability to navigate and influence stakeholders across large organisations.

 - Proactive ownership and comfort in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

Nice to Have

 - Experience with usage-based or API-driven products.

 - Background in AI, data platforms, developer tools, or creative technology.

 - Experience working with technical stakeholders such as engineering or product teams.

 - Experience scaling accounts in high-growth startups.

Note: this body covers the three Customer Success roles — EMEA (London), EMEA German-speaking (London), and Germany (Munich). The two German roles add: native or fluent German required.

jobs.title: Lifecycle & Growth Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Luma is looking for a Growth Marketer to own the systems and experiences that turn interest into customers, and customers into more engaged, higher-value customers.

You'll own the full conversion journey across our website, landing pages, onboarding, lifecycle marketing, and retention. You'll be responsible for understanding where people get stuck, figuring out what will move them, and building the programs and experiences that make it happen.

This is a highly cross-functional role. You'll work closely with Product, Design, Sales, and Marketing to improve everything from the first website visit to trial conversion, activation, expansion, and re-engagement. You'll combine strong marketing instincts with analytical rigor: understanding the numbers, forming hypotheses, and then turning those hypotheses into better experiences.

We're looking for someone who can zoom out and see the funnel as a system, then zoom in and obsess over the words on a landing page, the timing of an email, or the friction in a signup flow. You’ll have an amazing instinct for what to say and when to say it.

You'll have support to execute campaigns and programs in our marketing tools. Your job is to determine what we should build, who it's for, why it should work, and how we'll know if it did.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN


CONVERSION & WEBSITE

 - Own conversion strategy across the Luma website and key acquisition surfaces

 - Identify and prioritize opportunities across the website funnel, from first visit through signup, trial, and purchase

 - Develop and optimize landing pages for campaigns, products, audiences, and use cases

 - Partner with Design and Web to improve messaging, information architecture, CTAs, and conversion paths

 - Develop and run a structured CRO program: establish hypotheses, prioritize tests, analyze results, and continuously improve conversion

 - Use behavioral and funnel data to understand where users drop off and why

 - Analyze conversion across tiers, plans, and customer segments to identify opportunities for growth


LIFECYCLE MARKETING

 - Own lifecycle strategy across the customer journey: nurture, trial conversion, onboarding, activation, engagement, cross-sell, expansion, and re-engagement

 - Design segmented, sequenced programs that move people toward the next meaningful action, rather than simply sending more email

 - Develop lifecycle journeys across email and in-product surfaces in partnership with Product

 - Partner with Sales and Growth to connect lifecycle programs to the actual customer journey and buying process

 - Establish segmentation and behavioral triggers that make lifecycle communication increasingly relevant and personalized

 - Build experiments that increase activation, retention, expansion/upgrades, and customer engagement


EXPERIMENTATION & GROWTH

 - Establish a clear growth experimentation roadmap across website, pricing, conversion, and lifecycle

 - Define hypotheses, success metrics, and testing methodology

 - Analyze performance and translate data into actionable insights

 - Build a culture of continuous experimentation rather than one-off optimization

 - Identify the highest-leverage opportunities across the funnel and prioritize accordingly


SYSTEMS & MEASUREMENT

 - Own the strategy and architecture of our lifecycle and conversion systems

 - Define the funnel and lifecycle metrics that matter, including visitor-to-signup, signup-to-trial, trial-to-paid, activation, engagement, expansion, and re-engagement

 - Build reporting that gives the team a clear view of where growth is coming from and where we're losing it

 - Continuously improve our systems, processes, and measurement as the company scales


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 8+ years in growth, lifecycle, CRM, conversion, or related marketing roles, ideally with experience spanning both PLG and sales-assisted motions

 - A track record of improving measurable funnel outcomes, not just launching campaigns

 - Experience with lifecycle marketing, segmentation, experimentation, and marketing automation

 - Strong understanding of website conversion and landing pages.

 - Strong analytical instincts, you're comfortable digging into funnel data, identifying patterns, and turning them into hypotheses

 - Strong editorial instincts, you know that better conversion isn't just about buttons and mechanics; it's about getting the message, value proposition, and experience right

 - Excellent writer and communicator who can personally develop messaging when needed

 - Bonus points if you’ve worked with Braze, Hubspot, Sanity, Vercel, Linear

 - Curious about the product and willing to understand how it works, why it matters, and who it's for

 - Highly autonomous and comfortable owning an ambiguous, evolving area

 - Equally comfortable setting strategy and getting into the details




LUMA AT A GLANCE:

Luma AI is a frontier research lab and an AI-native product company. We're building creative agents that expand what creative professionals can imagine and make. AI is a story that gets told on social first, and Luma's is one of the best there is to tell. This is a rare shot to own that narrative, define a category, and make Luma the brand the creative world can't stop watching.

jobs.title: Director of Customer Success [EMEA]
jobs.description:
This is a hands-on leadership role at the center of our EMEA Customer Success organization. 

You'll lead a small, senior team of 5 with the intention to double to 10 in the next 12 months.  

Based from London, your team sit locally along with a growing team in Munich and possibly Riyadh in future working with enterprise customers across EMEA.




WHERE YOU COME IN

You'll carry formal accountability for your team's performance, development, hiring, and day-to-day effectiveness — and you'll stay personally engaged in the region's most strategic accounts, at the level where a senior voice changes the outcome. Your core mandate is to turn a set of excellent individual practices into one operating system: the account planning, escalation, and reporting structures that let the team scale without a proportional rise in headcount.

This fits someone who wants to lead from close range rather than inherit a large, already-built org. If you're looking for a defined playbook or a steady renewal book to protect, this isn't that — you'll be building the playbook as you go.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Lead the EMEA Customer Success team — owning hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and career development for a small group of senior CSMs.

 - Stay personally engaged in the region's most strategic accounts, holding senior relationships directly and stepping in when a situation needs a decision at your level.

 - Decide where the team's time goes: which accounts warrant depth, what account enablement work is worth the investment, and what should become a repeatable, templated motion versus a bespoke one-off.

 - Build the account planning, escalation, and reporting processes that let the team absorb more enterprise customers without adding headcount at the same rate.

 - Own performance outcomes for the accounts the team covers — net revenue retention, retention rates, health score distribution, and escalation resolution — and report cleanly to leadership.

 - Grow usage inside existing accounts — across more teams, more markets, and more use cases

 - Partner cross-functionally with Sales on renewals and new-account expansion, with Forward Deployed Creatives on workflow adoption, and with Product on what customers in the region need built next.

 - Identify and develop talent — building a bench of strong individual contributors and emerging player-coaches who can grow with the organization.

 - Lead hiring for the team as it scales, setting an explicit bar for what "senior" looks like in EMEA Customer Success.

 - Set and maintain a high standard of execution across the team: account health, CRM hygiene, renewal management, expansion identification, and customer engagement quality.

 - Serve as a senior point of escalation for complex customer situations that have exceeded what the team can resolve independently.

 - Contribute to CS strategy alongside regional and functional leadership — bringing a ground-level view of team capability, customer patterns, and operational gaps into planning conversations.




WHO YOU ARE

 - 10+ years of experience in Customer Success or a closely related client-facing function, including substantial experience leading teams of senior individual contributors (not only early-career CSMs) with direct accountability for performance outcomes.

 - A proven people manager — you've built and developed CS teams, navigated performance conversations with directness and care, and have a track record of retention and growth among your reports.

 - A record of personally holding senior relationships at large enterprise or agency accounts, including the conversations that go badly.

 - Evidence you've made a team's work repeatable — you've taken a function running on effort and given it a system, and can say what you cut to get there.

 - Strong operational leader — you build reliable execution systems, hold teams to consistent standards, and are comfortable owning outcome metrics rather than just activity metrics.

 - Presence — you can lead people who already know their job well, in a region removed from headquarters, and earn their respect quickly while holding your own point of view.

 - Comfortable operating across multiple markets within the region while working closely with a leadership team based elsewhere.

 - Effective cross-functional partner — you work well with Sales, Product, and GTM leaders and understand how CS fits into the broader revenue motion.

 - Comfortable operating in a scaling environment where team structure, tooling, and process are still being refined — you improve the system rather than waiting for it to be finished.




WHAT SETS YOU APART

 - Experience building or significantly scaling a CS function at a high-growth startup — including hiring, process development, and team structure design.

 - Fluency with marketers — real time spent working with advertising agencies or brand marketing teams, whether from a software vendor, a media owner, an ad tech or martech company, or from inside an agency or brand.

 - Background at a creative technology, generative AI, or product-led growth company.

 - Track record of developing CS managers or leads from IC backgrounds — not just hiring experienced managers externally.

 - Deep familiarity with CRM and customer success tooling, and a point of view on how to use data to manage team performance.

Nice to Have

 - An additional European language.

 - Experience at a creative software, martech, or ad tech company selling into agency groups and global brands.

 - Familiarity with adjacent, newly-opened markets relevant to the region's growth (e.g. the Middle East).
